messages.subject: gl.ibd query
parts:
Hey all, 

I was wanting to run an IBD test on individuals rather than populations. Is this possible with the gl.ibd function? 
If the gl.ibd function only works for populations and not individuals, does anyone have a suggestion for another IBD function that would work on individuals?


Kind regards, 

Tegan Dinsdale.

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] gl.ibd query
parts:
Hi Tegan,

 

You basically could run an ibd by “hand” using for example an individual based distance measure e.g.

 

  1. Proportion of Shared Alleles

 

 

1-gl.propShared(gl)  #dartR version 1.5.5

 

And then do a mantel test of the lower triangle of the matrices (gendistance) against eulidean Distance.

 

Euclidean distances are simply calculated via dist (gl@other$latlong)

 

Though you may want to project your coordinates so you have distances in meters.

 

You can find such a projection on my dartRWorkshop github pages (at the end of the Katoomba workshop pdf for example).

 

Cheers, Bernd

messages.subject: RE: [dartR] gl.ibd query
parts:
Hi Arthur,

 

Not sure if that works as you cannot calculate Fsts for single individuals. So what I had in mind was:

 

Cheers, Bernd

 

Again projected coordinates would be preferred here.

gd <- 1-gl.propShared(testset.gl)

ed <- as.matrix(dist(testset.gl@other$latlong))

plot(as.dist(gd)~ as.dist(ed))

library(vegan)

mantel(ed,gd)

Mantel statistic based on Pearson's product-moment correlation 
 
Call:
mantel(xdis = ed, ydis = gd) 
 
Mantel statistic r: 0.6036 
      Significance: 0.001 
 
Upper quantiles of permutations (null model):
   90%    95%  97.5%    99% 
0.0647 0.0827 0.1110 0.1261 
Permutation: free
Number of permutations: 999

Hi Tegan,

 

gl.reassign.pop(gl, as.pop="id")
